name: Upgrade a cluster with kubeadm (real apply)
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration (25%). The real thing most benches only let you READ: actually run `kubeadm upgrade plan` and `kubeadm upgrade apply` to move a control plane up a minor version, then upgrade the kubelet. Runs on a dedicated THROWAWAY cluster ('kindlab-upgrade', pinned at v1.35.0) so the real upgrade never touches your main cluster. ⚠ Point kubectl at this lab's cluster: export KUBECONFIG=<repo>/.state/kindlab-upgrade.kubeconfig. Node: docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane. The target-version binaries are pre-staged at /opt/k136 on that node (on kind this stands in for `apt-get install kubeadm/kubelet=<ver>`).

questions.title: Upgrade the control plane (kubeadm upgrade apply)
questions.teach:
A cluster upgrade is **control plane first, kubelets second**, and only **one minor version at a time**. On each control-plane node you upgrade the `kubeadm` tool, check the plan, then apply: `kubeadm upgrade plan` (read-only) → `kubeadm upgrade apply vX.Y.Z`. kubeadm pulls the new component images and re-renders the static-pod manifests; the kubelet restarts the control plane on the new version.

**Gotcha:** `kubeadm upgrade apply <ver>` must be run by a **matching** `kubeadm` binary — upgrade the tool first. On kind there are no apt packages, so the new binaries are staged at `/opt/k136`; `cp /opt/k136/kubeadm /usr/bin/kubeadm` is the stand-in for `apt-get install -y kubeadm=<ver>`.
questions.prompt:
This lab's cluster `kindlab-upgrade` is at **v1.35.0**. Upgrade its control plane to **v1.36.1** on node `kindlab-upgrade-control-plane`: install the staged kubeadm, read the plan, then apply.

First: `export KUBECONFIG=<repo>/.state/kindlab-upgrade.kubeconfig`.

Target: the `kube-apiserver-kindlab-upgrade-control-plane` static pod runs image `…:v1.36.1`.
questions.hint: On the node: `docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane cp /opt/k136/kubeadm /usr/bin/kubeadm` (installs the new tool), then `docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane kubeadm upgrade plan`, then `docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane kubeadm upgrade apply v1.36.1 -y`. It pulls images and upgrades the static pods (~2-4 min).
questions.solution:
N=kindlab-upgrade-control-plane

# 1) install the new kubeadm (kind stand-in for: apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.36.1)
docker exec $N cp /opt/k136/kubeadm /usr/bin/kubeadm
docker exec $N kubeadm version -o short            # v1.36.1

# 2) read the plan (what it would upgrade)
docker exec $N kubeadm upgrade plan

# 3) apply the upgrade — pulls new images, re-renders control-plane static pods
docker exec $N kubeadm upgrade apply v1.36.1 -y

# verify the apiserver image bumped
export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/.state/kindlab-upgrade.kubeconfig"
kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-$N -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'; echo

verification.description: control plane upgraded to the target version (kube-apiserver image)

questions.eli5:
Upgrading a Kubernetes cluster is like renovating a building while people still live in it — you do it floor by floor, in order, and only one storey at a time. The rule: **control plane (the management floor) first, worker kubelets second**, and never skip a minor version (1.35 → 1.36, not 1.35 → 1.37).

The foreman for the upgrade is the **`kubeadm`** tool. But you must give the foreman the *new* blueprint before he can build the new floor — so step one is to **install the new `kubeadm`** itself. On a normal machine that's `apt-get install kubeadm=1.36.1`; on this kind node the new tools are already sitting at `/opt/k136`, so you just copy `kubeadm` into place.

Then you ask the foreman two things:
- `kubeadm upgrade plan` — "what would you change?" (read-only preview).
- `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.36.1` — "do it." kubeadm downloads the new control-plane images, rewrites the static-pod manifests, and the kubelet restarts the apiserver/scheduler/controller-manager/etcd on the new version.

**Watch out for:**

- **Upgrade the `kubeadm` tool FIRST.** `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.36.1` must be run by a v1.36.1 kubeadm, or it refuses.
- **One minor at a time.** You can't jump 1.35 → 1.37; go 1.35 → 1.36 first.
- **`plan` changes nothing** — it's a preview. `apply` is the real action.
- **It takes a few minutes** and pulls images — be patient; the API blips as each static pod restarts.
- **This is only the control plane.** The kubelet is still old until step 2.
- Make sure `KUBECONFIG` points at **this lab's** cluster, not your main one.
questions.deepDive:
## kubeadm control-plane upgrade — full rundown

### Mental model
Upgrade order is strict: **kubeadm tool → control plane (`kubeadm upgrade apply`) → kubelet/kubectl → other nodes (`kubeadm upgrade node`)** — and only **one minor version per hop**. `apply` runs on the **first** control-plane node; additional control-plane nodes use `kubeadm upgrade node`.

### The real sequence (per control-plane node)
```bash
# 1. upgrade the kubeadm binary to the target version
apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.36.1-*   # real nodes
# (this kind lab: cp /opt/k136/kubeadm /usr/bin/kubeadm)
kubeadm version -o short            # v1.36.1

# 2. plan (read-only) then apply
kubeadm upgrade plan
kubeadm upgrade apply v1.36.1 -y    # pulls images, re-renders static pods
```
`apply` uploads the new config, upgrades etcd + CoreDNS + kube-proxy, renews certs, and re-renders `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/*` so the kubelet restarts each component on the new image.

### plan vs apply
| Command | Changes cluster? | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `kubeadm upgrade plan [ver]` | ❌ no | preview versions + component targets |
| `kubeadm upgrade apply <ver>` | ✅ yes | upgrade this control-plane node |
| `kubeadm upgrade node` | ✅ yes | other control-plane nodes + worker kubelet config |

### Version skew rules (why order matters)
- **kubeadm** must be ≥ the target and the same minor as the version you apply.
- **kubelet** may be up to **3 minors older** than the apiserver (so old kubelet + new control plane is fine transiently — you upgrade it next).
- **Never skip a minor.** 1.35 → 1.36 → 1.37, one hop at a time.

### Worker / node upgrade (step 2 covers the kubelet)
```bash
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets   # from a control-plane / admin context
kubeadm upgrade node                        # on the node (updates local kubelet config)
# upgrade kubelet + kubectl packages, then:
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl uncordon <node>
```
(This single-node lab folds the kubelet upgrade into step 2.)

### Verify
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-<node> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'  # :v1.36.1
kubectl get nodes                      # control-plane still shows old kubelet until step 2
kubeadm upgrade plan                   # now reports you're on the target
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Upgrade `kubeadm` before `apply`** — mismatched tool version refuses.
- **`plan` is safe/read-only**; only `apply` mutates.
- **One minor at a time** — jumping minors fails preflight.
- **Images are pulled at apply time** — needs registry access; slow on first run.
- **Control plane ≠ done** — the node's kubelet is still the old version until you upgrade it (step 2).
- On multi-master, only the first node uses `apply`; the rest use `kubeadm upgrade node`.

### Quick reference
```bash
N=kindlab-upgrade-control-plane
docker exec $N cp /opt/k136/kubeadm /usr/bin/kubeadm     # "install" new kubeadm
docker exec $N kubeadm upgrade plan
docker exec $N kubeadm upgrade apply v1.36.1 -y
```

questions.title: Upgrade the kubelet
questions.teach:
After the control plane is on the new version, each node's **kubelet** still runs the old one — upgrade it too. The real flow: upgrade the `kubelet` (and `kubectl`) packages, then `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet`. On a real worker you'd `kubectl drain` it first and `uncordon` after; a single control-plane node skips the drain.

**Gotcha:** the node's reported version (`kubectl get nodes`) only changes **after the kubelet restarts** on the new binary. Install the binary, then restart — give it ~15-30s to re-register at the new version.
questions.prompt:
The control plane is now v1.36.1 but `kubectl get nodes` still shows the kubelet at v1.35.0. Upgrade the kubelet on `kindlab-upgrade-control-plane`: install the staged kubelet (and kubectl), then daemon-reload and restart the kubelet.

Target: node `kindlab-upgrade-control-plane` reports `kubeletVersion` **v1.36.1**.
questions.hint: On the node: `docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane cp /opt/k136/kubelet /usr/bin/kubelet` (and `/opt/k136/kubectl /usr/bin/kubectl`), then `docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane systemctl daemon-reload` and `docker exec kindlab-upgrade-control-plane systemctl restart kubelet`. Wait ~20s, then `kubectl get nodes` (lab kubeconfig).
questions.solution:
N=kindlab-upgrade-control-plane

# install the new kubelet + kubectl (stand-in for: apt-get install -y kubelet=1.36.1 kubectl=1.36.1)
docker exec $N cp /opt/k136/kubelet /usr/bin/kubelet
docker exec $N cp /opt/k136/kubectl /usr/bin/kubectl

# reload systemd and restart the kubelet on the new binary
docker exec $N systemctl daemon-reload
docker exec $N systemctl restart kubelet

# node re-registers at the new version in ~15-30s
export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/.state/kindlab-upgrade.kubeconfig"
kubectl get nodes -o wide     # VERSION -> v1.36.1

verification.description: kubelet upgraded to the target version on the node

questions.eli5:
You renovated the management floor (the control plane), but the building's caretaker on this floor — the **kubelet** — is still using his old manual. Until you hand him the new one and he clocks back in, the floor still *reports* itself as the old version.

So you **install the new kubelet** (on a real node: `apt-get install kubelet=1.36.1`; here: copy `/opt/k136/kubelet` into place), tell systemd to re-read its service files (`daemon-reload`), and **restart the kubelet**. He picks up the new manual, re-registers with the cluster, and now `kubectl get nodes` shows the node at v1.36.1.

On a real worker node you'd also **drain** it first (move workloads off) and **uncordon** it after — polite maintenance. A single control-plane node in this lab skips the drain.

**Watch out for:**

- **The node version changes only after the kubelet RESTARTS** — installing the binary alone does nothing; you must restart.
- **`daemon-reload` then `restart`** — reload picks up any unit changes, restart swaps the running kubelet.
- **Give it ~15-30s** to re-register; don't panic if `get nodes` lags briefly.
- On a real worker: **drain before, uncordon after** — don't forget the uncordon or nothing schedules there.
- The kubelet may be a few minors behind the apiserver safely, but you should match them when upgrading.
questions.deepDive:
## Upgrading the kubelet — full rundown

### Mental model
The control-plane upgrade (step 1) does **not** touch the node's kubelet binary. Each node is upgraded separately: install the new `kubelet` (+`kubectl`) package, reload systemd, restart the kubelet. The node's `kubeletVersion` updates only once the **new kubelet process is running**.

### The real per-node sequence
```bash
# (worker nodes: drain first, from an admin context)
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

# on the node: refresh kubelet config for this node (kubeadm-managed clusters)
kubeadm upgrade node

# install the new kubelet + kubectl
apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubelet=1.36.1-* kubectl=1.36.1-*
# (this kind lab: cp /opt/k136/kubelet /usr/bin/kubelet ; cp /opt/k136/kubectl /usr/bin/kubectl)

# restart the kubelet on the new binary
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart kubelet

# (worker nodes) allow scheduling again
kubectl uncordon <node>
```
This single control-plane-node lab skips drain/uncordon (nowhere to evict to) and folds `kubeadm upgrade node`'s kubelet-config step into the control-plane upgrade already done.

### Why restart is mandatory
`systemctl restart kubelet` swaps the running process for the new binary. Until then the node keeps advertising the old `kubeletVersion` in its status — the installed-but-not-restarted binary is inert. `daemon-reload` first makes systemd re-read unit/drop-in files (harmless if unchanged, required if they changed).

### Verify
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o wide                 # VERSION column -> v1.36.1
kubectl get node <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}'   # v1.36.1
systemctl status kubelet                  # active (running)
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Install ≠ upgrade** — the version only changes after `systemctl restart kubelet`.
- **`daemon-reload` before `restart`** when the unit/drop-ins changed.
- **Workers: drain before, uncordon after.** Forgetting uncordon leaves the node `SchedulingDisabled`.
- **If the kubelet won't come back**, check `journalctl -u kubelet -e` — a bad config or binary mismatch keeps the node `NotReady` (🧰 Node toolbox).
- **Match kubelet to the control plane** when upgrading, even though a few minors of skew is tolerated.

### Quick reference
```bash
N=kindlab-upgrade-control-plane
docker exec $N cp /opt/k136/kubelet /usr/bin/kubelet
docker exec $N systemctl daemon-reload && docker exec $N systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl get nodes -o wide     # v1.36.1
```
